text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for SLO: ingestion-service p99 latency > 1200ms across eu-west :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Triggered PD incident INC123456 — urgency: high — current count: 48 alerts in 5m — escalation policy: oncall-eng -> eng-sre -> eng-runtime
sam: acked in PD, picking this up. I’m oncall now. First look: Grafana shows a sharp p99 spike starting ~6581112000 UTC, CPU on gpu-sidecars normal, but request queue depth jumped.
tia: @sam thx — any correlation with recent deploys? I saw a canary rollout for model v2 at 07:10 UTC.
sam: good call — I see deployment tag model=v2 on ~07:08. Canary pods in eu-west show higher tail latency.
leo: jumping in — model v2 has a quantized path change, possible KV cache behavior. KV hit rate for eu-west dropped from 92% -> 18% at the same time.
maria: product note: some Dedicated customers in EU may notice slow completions, but hosted API mostly degraded for long sequences. Flagging support channels.
sam: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) pause canary rollout 2) route eu-west traffic back to model v1 3) warm KV cache for nodes if possible. Who can run routing?
leo: I can flip routing. Command I’ll run: `reconf route set --region eu-west --model model-v1 --weight 100`
tia: I’ll pause rollout: `kubectl -n inference pause rollout model-v2-canary` and post rollout events.
incident-bot: Action logged: rollout paused by tia at 6581112185 UTC.
leo: routing change applied, verifying traffic now showing 100% v1 for eu-west.
sam: monitoring… p99 dropping but still high, now 1.05s. Queue depth falling.
maria: support FYI sent: "We observed a model canary causing tail latency for long sequences in eu-west; routing rollback in progress."
leo: KV cache hit rate slowly climbing back to 85% after routing change — looks like the v2 inference path cold-started many caches and caused evictions.
sam: can we throttle long-sequence requests temporarily? That might reduce tail.
tia: we have a short-term limiter: `configctl set rate-limit prefix_long_seq 30rps --region eu-west` — setting now.
incident-bot: Rate limit change applied by tia at 6581112250 UTC.
leo: after limiter, p99 down to ~650ms, p95 stable ~120ms. Queue depths normalized.
sam: ok taking incident to triage stage. Please post short notes: root cause hypothesis = canary model variant triggered KV cache churn + cold path for quantized kernels -> tail latency spike.
maria: creating incident ticket for customer comms and CS follow-up.
tia: runbook links: https://intranet/runbooks/latency-tail and https://intranet/deploys/model-canary-playbook — follow for postmortem steps.
leo: suggest follow-ups: 1) add canary warmup to ensure KV cache population 2) add rollout gating for latency regressions 3) increase autopager suppression threshold for brief cache churns.
sam: agreed. Oncall handoff — I’ll keep monitoring for 20 more mins then hand to next oncall if stable. If p99 < 700ms for 15m, we mark resolved.
oncall-rotation-bot: Next oncall: @alex starts at 6581113600 UTC.
incident-bot: PagerDuty INC123456 status: acknowledged by sam — escalation paused.
sam: final note before handoff: no customer-facing errors, only increased latency for long sequences; dedicated capacity customers unaffected except some with eu-west proximity. Will write summary in the incident ticket and start postmortem draft.
leo: tagging infra to review KV eviction thresholds: @eng-infra.
maria: support ready for comms once postmortem has timeline.
sam: closing chat — keeping PD open until stabilization window complete. Thanks team :thumbsup:
